fixes.explanation: Egypt, huh? Nice guess, but Joshua's not looking that far back. He says, "If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!" (Joshua 7:7). That's the river they just crossed. I think he's so upset that he's wishing the crossing undone.

They "…spread them out before the LORD." (Joshua 7:23). Achan hid that stuff in a hole in the ground inside his tent. Now the cloak, the silver and the gold bar are laid out in the open like a yard sale nobody wanted. Verse 22 says it was all there with the silver underneath, just as he said. I know a little about being stuffed out of sight, baker, and I bet it never feels as safe as it looks.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
The passage does not say the trip started on the Jordan’s far bank. Joshua wishes they had stayed on the other side; he does not identify where their trip began.
Saying Achan hid the things like a secret he never expected to explain gives him an expectation the passage does not state, without marking it as a guess.
